sentences.text: The largest known skull of this extinct fish may have reached approximately 10 cm in length.
Quasipetalichthys haikouensis is the only known species of the genus, and its fossils are found exclusively in the Haikou Formation in south-central China.
This animal belongs to the class Placodermi, a group of armored fish.
Quasipetalichthys is considered a basal member of the Petalichthyidae, though some researchers once called it aberrant.
Eurycaraspis is placed in the family Quasipetalichthyidae as a sister taxon to Quasipetalichthys.
Fossils were found alongside antiarch placoderms like Bothriolepis sinensis and Hunanolepis.
Fossils date to the Middle Devonian Givetian stage, placing the animal's existence between 387.95 and 372.15 million years ago.
The presence of Devonian plants alongside these fossils suggests Quasipetalichthys lived in a near-shore or freshwater environment.
